GenerateMoveStateMachine.issue: BRANCH ADD ORDER IS REVERSED. Inklet.cs:73-74 adds the live RAND branch's two arms in the order PIERCING_GAZE_MOVE (moveState3) then WHIRLWIND_MOVE (moveState2), both CannotRepeat with weight 1f; inklets.py:62-65 rolls `weighted_branch_pick(..., ['WHIRLWIND', 'PIERCING_GAZE'], [1, 1])` -- the opposite order. Add order is OBSERVABLE (monster_state_machine step 14: one NextFloat(total) then subtract-and-walk in add order), so with two equal weights the SAME draw resolves to the OPPOSITE move on every single roll. Executed, `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py inklet`: 20000 rolls on identically seeded MonsterAi streams, **agreement 0/20000 (0.00%)**, with the marginal split preserved (sim 10022 WHIRLWIND / 9978 PIERCING_GAZE; game 10022 PIERCING_GAZE / 9978 WHIRLWIND) -- which is exactly why a distribution check alone would have cleared it. Executed end-to-end, `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py branch`: over 40 turns on seeds b01/b02/b03 and both is_middle arms, the port and a reference machine built with the C# parameters diverge at the FIRST JAB->RAND transition every time, while consuming the identical number of MonsterAi draws (20 vs 20) -- so the divergence is pure move content, not stream drift. Observable: the player sees the wrong telegraphed intent and takes 10 damage instead of 2x3, or vice versa; a replay diverges on turn 2. LIVE, both sides reachable on ported content (rule 6): 'inklets_normal' is in the ported overgrowth NORMAL pool (rooms.py:99), the encounter builds three Inklets with the middle one flagged (inklets.py:70-73, matching InkletsNormal.cs:13-25), and every Inklet reaches RAND on its second turn. Same BUG CLASS as monster_state_machine G1 (a port misreading a RandomBranchState declaration) but a DIFFERENT mechanism -- G1 is about integer arguments read as weights; this is branch ORDER -- so G1 is cited, not re-verdicted, and this is a new unit-level gap. Not covered by the existing pin: test/test_monster_branch_audit.py::TestInkletMoveSequence::test_jab_rolls_exactly_one_draw_matching_game_primitive computes its own expectation with the SAME reversed order (test file lines 68-84, verified by reading it), so it locks the defect in rather than catching it, and its class docstring asserts 'a true 50/50 every time' -- true of the marginal, silent about the per-draw mapping.
